explanation: RAII is a fundamental C++ programming idiom where resource management is tied to the object's lifetime.  Resources (like memory, files, network connections, mutexes) are acquired in the object's constructor and released in its destructor. This ensures resources are always released, even in the presence of exceptions, preventing resource leaks and improving program robustness.  It's a cornerstone of exception safety and promotes cleaner, more maintainable code.  Best practices involve using RAII consistently for all resource management, avoiding manual resource handling whenever possible.
